International Prohibitionist View of US Medical Marijuana Battle

From the Hassela Nordic Network in Stockholm

THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE ASKED JUDGE TO SHUT DOWN CALIFORNIA´S MEDICAL MARIJUANA CLUBS FOR VIOLATION OF FEDERAL DRUG LAWS

On Tuesday, the U.S. Department of Justice made it perfectly clear that California´s so-called ‘medical marijuana’ clubs should be shut down for violation of federal drug laws.

"What this case is about, make no mistake about it, is upholding federal law. A state initiative cannot supplant the will of the people of the United States", government attorney Mark Quinlivan said.

On Tuesday, The Justice Department planned to file suit in a San Francisco federal court demanding that six clubs be closed down. Supporters of the marijuana clubs, a few politicians and San Francisco´s district attorney gathered for a march and rally in front of the U.S. Courthouse, demanding that marijuana be treated like any other medicine.

After hearing arguments from both sides, Judge Charles Breyer told attorneys to file final legal briefs by April 15, after which he would make a ruling.

Federal officials on Tuesday said marijuana club operations were an "outright and flagrant" violation of the 1970 Controlled Substances Act, under which Congress categorized marijuana as a dangerous drug.

"We have requested these injunctions in order to send a clear message regarding the illegality of marijuana cultivation and distribution", U.S. District Attorney Michael Yamaguchi said.

On Monday, police in San Jose arrested Peter Baez, the co-founder of the Santa Clara County Medical Cannabis Center (!), charging him with a felony count of illegally selling drugs without a prescription.

HNN-comment: Of course these clubs should be closed down as they are part of a strategy to legalize cannabis. The so-called ‘medical marijuana’ distribution is just part of a plan to first legalize marijuana and, later on, other drugs.

The strategy has been clearly outlined by IAL, CORA and the Transnational Radical Party and in internal documents distributed to members of these groups it is clearly stated that these groups want to achieve a legalization of all drugs. However, they realize that the ordinary citizen won´t buy the idea of legalizing all drugs immediately, so they´ve decided starting with the cannabis issue. In Europe, CORA has declared that Italy will be the primary target for their legalization efforts as Italy, according to CORA, has the weakest political structure.

The following was said in an internal message, dated November 10, 1997, sent to CORA supporters "Although we are more than ever convinced that the basic aspect of the drug issue remains the trafficking and in particular the traffic of the so-called hard drugs, and latterly of synthetic drugs, and that therefore our goal is and remains to be the legalization of all drugs, we think that with the legalization of hashish we can break an important taboo and create the possibility for achieving our ultimate goal. We are also convinced that Italy represents the weakest link in the chain of the prohibitionist system in Europe, that is to say, today in Italy there exists the political conditions for fundamental reform of drug laws"..."If you are available to participate in the actions of civil disobedience in Italy and furthermore to organise actions in other European countries in the future, we would be very happy to hear from you and to be able to count on your active participation in this phase of development."
